title: AI-predicted spatial transcriptomics unlocks breast cancer biomarkers from pathology
what_it_strengthens: This is the closest high-impact precedent: H&E-predicted spatial transcriptomics enabling biomarker discovery.
best_use: Foreground in Fig 1 and presub; state that Paper 2 applies the logic to thyroid DM1/RAI.
boundary: Breast cancer precedent, not thyroid; do not claim same model or same biomarker class.
source_kind: local PDF plus web DOI check

title: Integrating spatial gene expression and breast tumour morphology via deep learning
what_it_strengthens: ST-Net established local gene-expression prediction from H&E as a serious biomedical-engineering problem.
best_use: Use as the classic ST prediction precedent.
boundary: Breast cancer and paired ST training; not a thyroid validation.

title: A deep learning model to predict RNA-Seq expression of tumours from whole slide images
what_it_strengthens: HE2RNA supports the broad claim that WSI morphology contains transcriptomic signal.
best_use: Use for the general H&E-to-RNA premise and spatialization precedent.
boundary: Bulk RNA labels, not true thyroid spatial RNA.

title: Benchmarking the translational potential of spatial gene expression prediction from histology
what_it_strengthens: Provides editor-facing precedent that the field now judges H&E-to-spatial expression by benchmarking and translational guardrails.
best_use: Use to justify honest caveats, held-out testing, and random-module controls.
boundary: Benchmark paper; does not validate DM1 biology.

title: Robust and interpretable prediction of gene markers and cell types from spatial transcriptomics data
what_it_strengthens: STimage makes robustness, uncertainty, interpretability, and multi-platform validation part of the current field standard.
best_use: Use to explain why Paper 2 co-locates caveats with results.
boundary: Do not imply Paper 2 performs STimage-level uncertainty modeling.

title: sCellST predicts single-cell gene expression from H&E images
what_it_strengthens: Moves the field from spot-scale prediction toward cell-level molecular interpretation from H&E.
best_use: Use as a frontier reference; Paper 2 stays spot/module-level.
boundary: Not thyroid; not used by our pipeline.

title: STPath: a generative foundation model for integrating spatial transcriptomics and whole-slide images
what_it_strengthens: Shows that ST+WSI foundation modeling is now an explicit digital-medicine direction.
best_use: Use to position Paper 2 as a disease-focused biomarker application rather than a new universal model.
boundary: Do not claim our model has STPath-scale pretraining or organ breadth.

title: Inferring super-resolution tissue architecture by integrating spatial transcriptomics with histology
what_it_strengthens: iStar supports the spatial-resolution argument: histology can improve molecular maps beyond spot resolution.
best_use: Use as adjacent method precedent.
boundary: It integrates measured ST; Paper 2 infers thyroid DM1 spatial state from H&E features.

title: Self-supervised learning for characterising histomorphological diversity and spatial RNA expression prediction across 23 human tissue types
what_it_strengthens: Supports the general tissue-diversity framing for self-supervised histology representations.
best_use: Use to keep H&E framing broad without claiming pan-disease validation.
boundary: General tissue paper; not thyroid-specific.

title: AI-enabled virtual spatial proteomics from histopathology for interpretable biomarker discovery in lung cancer
what_it_strengthens: HEX is a major clinical precedent that H&E can generate virtual spatial molecular maps with outcome relevance.
best_use: Use as the strongest translational analog; Paper 2 is RNA/thyroid, not proteomics/lung.
boundary: Do not claim equal clinical validation or immunotherapy response prediction.

title: Classification and mutation prediction from non-small cell lung cancer histopathology images using deep learning
what_it_strengthens: Classic proof that H&E can predict molecular alterations from routine slides.
best_use: Use as historical root of image-to-molecular biomarkers.
boundary: Mutation prediction is not transcriptomic/spatial prediction.

title: Pan-cancer image-based detection of clinically actionable genetic alterations
what_it_strengthens: Shows that routine FFPE H&E can reflect a broad range of molecular alterations across cancers.
best_use: Use for generality of molecular information in histology.
boundary: Do not imply Paper 2 is pan-cancer.

title: Pan-cancer computational histopathology reveals mutations, tumor composition and prognosis
what_it_strengthens: Supports the idea that histology features correlate with mutations, tumor composition, expression, and prognosis.
best_use: Use to frame tumor composition and spatially resolved morphology.
boundary: Pan-cancer association, not thyroid DM1 validation.

title: Data-efficient and weakly supervised computational pathology on whole-slide images
what_it_strengthens: CLAM legitimizes attention/MIL-style WSI learning with slide-level labels and localization.
best_use: Use in Methods/architecture justification.
boundary: Method precedent, not biological validation.

title: Clinical-grade computational pathology using weakly supervised deep learning on whole slide images
what_it_strengthens: Shows clinical-grade weakly supervised WSI AI at scale.
best_use: Use sparingly for WSI AI validation ethos and scale expectations.
boundary: Not molecular prediction.

title: Towards a general-purpose foundation model for computational pathology
what_it_strengthens: UNI is the core model precedent and directly matches Paper 2's feature backbone.
best_use: Foreground in Methods, Fig 1, and data-use table.
boundary: Do not claim we invented UNI or trained a foundation model.

title: A visual-language foundation model for computational pathology
what_it_strengthens: CONCH supports pathology foundation-model maturation and transferable representations.
best_use: Use as context in the foundation-model paragraph.
boundary: Not used in current Paper 2 results.

title: A whole-slide foundation model for digital pathology from real-world data
what_it_strengthens: Prov-GigaPath supports whole-slide context and real-world pretraining as field direction.
best_use: Use as field context, especially if discussing external robustness.
boundary: Not our backbone unless explicitly tested.

title: A foundation model for clinical-grade computational pathology and rare cancers detection
what_it_strengthens: Virchow supports large-scale pathology FM claims and rare-cancer utility.
best_use: Use in impact paragraph only as field context.
boundary: Not our model; do not imply rare-cancer validation.

title: High-Spatial-Resolution Multi-Omics Sequencing via Deterministic Barcoding in Tissue
what_it_strengthens: DBiT-seq is the wet-lab spatial multi-omics root behind the user's 2026 epi-Patho-DBiT precedent.
best_use: Use as spatial-omics lineage reference.
boundary: Experimental spatial omics, not computational H&E inference.

title: Spatially decoding genotype-associated epigenetic landscapes in human lymphoma FFPE tissues via epi-Patho-DBiT
what_it_strengthens: The user-provided Nature Communications precedent: pathology/FFPE tissue can unlock spatial molecular disease biology.
best_use: Use as adjacent NC bridge: Paper 2 is the computational H&E front door.
boundary: Lymphoma epigenomics, not H&E-to-RNA AI and not thyroid.

title: Integrated Genomic Characterization of Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma
what_it_strengthens: TCGA-THCA is the core public thyroid reference and provides the genomics/pathology context.
best_use: Use in thyroid biology and dataset provenance.
boundary: Does not establish H&E-to-DM1 prediction by itself.

title: Genomic and transcriptomic hallmarks of poorly differentiated and anaplastic thyroid cancers
what_it_strengthens: Landa et al. anchors advanced thyroid dedifferentiation and transcriptomic context.
best_use: Use as thyroid/RAI biology reference and boundary for advanced disease.
boundary: Advanced PDTC/ATC, not H&E spatial prediction.

title: Biological insights and novel biomarker discovery through deep learning approaches in breast cancer histopathology
what_it_strengthens: Useful review language for histo-genomics and biomarker discovery from H&E.
best_use: Use only as background; prioritize primary papers in main claims.
boundary: Review article, not primary validation.
